images.alt:
A single red cedar-strip voyager canoe floats motionless on the mirror surface of Moraine Lake Alberta, its paddler a dark silhouette against an exploding sky of green and violet aurora borealis. The Valley of the Ten Peaks rises like jagged teeth around the lake, their granite faces catching faint phosphorescent glow from the dancing lights above. Snowfields cling to the upper reaches, glowing ethereal blue under the aurora. The water is so still that the entire scene is doubled — peaks, lights, and canoe reflected with perfect clarity. A lone loon creates a single V-shaped ripple near the bow. The air feels impossibly cold and silent, the kind of silence that hums. The composition evokes both the geological age of the mountains and the brief, fragile human moment within them.
Style: Long-exposure astrophotography, fine art landscape, cinematic nocturnal, painterly realism
Composition: Canoe placed at lower-third intersection, reflected peaks creating perfect vertical symmetry, aurora arcs framing the sky
Lighting: Ambient auroral glow as primary key light, faint starlight, no artificial light sources, deep cobalt twilight on water
Adjectives: Ethereal, silent, sublime, luminous, contemplative

record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: Uncovering the Experiences of Basti-Dwelling Adolescent Girls Who Menstruate in Hyderabad, India: #Protocol for a Multimethod Critical Qualitative #Study

external.description: Background: Rapid urbanization in India is straining the government’s capacity to provide basic amenities such as housing, sanitation, electricity, and water. One group of people who are deeply affected are adolescent girls who menstruate. In urban slums, referred to as bastis in Telugu and Hindi, this reality is worsened by spatial congestion and limited water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) resources. This #Study is situated in the populous slum colonies of Film Nagar, Hyderabad, where residents navigate precarious living conditions and a scarcity of basic amenities. Objective: In this context, we argue that menstrual experiences are profoundly shaped by an interplay of biological, sociopolitical, and environmental factors. This #Study aims to examine how these intersecting dimensions shape the menstrual experiences of slum-dwelling adolescent girls (aged 8‐18 years) in Film Nagar by understanding the (1) sociocultural and political discourse, (2) intergenerational household power dynamics, and (3) the enabling environment. Methods: Guided by biopolitics and poststructuralist feminist theory, we use a critical ethnographic approach involving intergenerational households (adolescent girls, mothers, fathers, and unmarried brothers aged 15‐24 years). Approximately 18‐28 informants across 5‐8 households will be recruited using maximum variation, purposive, and snowball sampling, targeting. Data generation includes rapport-building, participant observation (journaling, voice recordings, photography, or transect walks), document analysis, focus group discussions (FGDs), and in-depth interviews (IDIs). Analysis occurs concurrently using frame analysis: transcripts undergo value or narrative coding to inductively identify codes, followed by axial and selective coding to group codes into discourses interpreted through our theoretical framework, yielding dominant frames addressing each #Research question. record.text: JMIR Res Protocols: Clinical, Economic, and System-Level Outcomes of Bariatric Surgery in Adults: #Protocol for a Systematic Review

external.description: Background: Obesity affects approximately 880 million adults worldwide and carries substantial health, economic, and social consequences. Although bariatric surgery achieves sustained weight loss and metabolic improvement, existing systematic reviews largely predate 2020 and rarely integrate clinical, economic, and system-level perspectives within a single synthesis. Objective: This #Study aims to identify, critically appraise, and synthesize evidence published between 2020 and 2025 on the clinical effectiveness and economic impact of bariatric surgery in adults with obesity. A secondary, exploratory objective is to address system-level resource utilization, specifically length of stay, preoperative pathway duration, and outpatient care burden. Methods: This #Protocol follows the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis #Protocols) 2015 guidance and is registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO: CRD420261351022). Eligible studies will enroll adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m) undergoing any primary bariatric procedure, including Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB), sleeve gastrectomy (SG), one-anastomosis gastric bypass (OAGB), adjustable gastric banding (LAGB), and biliopancreatic diversion with or without duodenal switch (BPD±DS); revisional procedures are excluded as the index intervention. Eligible designs include #RCT #ClinicalTrials, cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, and economic evaluation studies published in English. MEDLINE (via PubMed), Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science will be searched using predefined, database-tailored strategies; records will be managed in Zotero (Corporation for #Digital Scholarship). A single primary reviewer will perform screening, extraction, and risk-of-bias (RoB) assessment, with at least 20% independently duplicated by a second reviewer, weighted toward full-text and included studies. RoB will be assessed with RoB 2 and ROBINS-I (Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions); economic evaluations will be appraised for completeness of reporting with the CHEERS (Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards) 2022 statement and for methodological quality with the CHEC (Consensus on Health Economic Criteria) checklist. The primary synthesis will be narrative; meta-analysis will be considered only where prespecified comparability criteria are met. Certainty of evidence will be rated using GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation). Results: This #Protocol describes a review that is currently in progress. Registration with PROSPERO was completed on April 15, 2026, and database searches were run on August 1, 2026, identifying 9400 records. Title-and-abstract screening is scheduled to begin on August 15, 2026. Data extraction and synthesis are expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with publication of the completed review anticipated in the first half of 2027. Conclusions: This #Protocol provides a transparent and reproducible methodology for an integrated, contemporary synthesis of the clinical, economic, and system-level outcomes of bariatric surgery in adults. The findings are intended to inform health policy, resource planning, and future #Research priorities.
